title: Measurement and feedforward circuits from quantum error correcting codes
abstract: Measurements and feedforward enhance the power of shallow quantum circuits, enabling the deterministic implementation of global unitary operations and the preparation of long-range entangled states. We establish a general correspondence between all such protocols and quantum error-correcting codes: the circuit preceding the measurements acts as an encoder, and unitary feedforward can eliminate post-selection if and only if the measurement projectors are detectable errors on the codespace. This correspondence provides a common framework for state preparation and implementation of global unitaries with measurements and feedforward, turning both into a code-design problem. For stabilizer codes with Pauli measurements, although the resulting operation can be non-Clifford, we show that its nonstabilizerness originates entirely from the encoder. We overcome this restriction using non-Pauli measurements or non-additive codes, constructing protocols that generate long-range nonstabilizerness while requiring only single-qubit unitary corrections.
summary: This paper develops a deep theoretical link between Measurement and Feedforward (CMF) quantum protocols and the theory of Quantum Error Correcting (QEC) codes. It shows that designing such protocols is equivalent to a code-design problem, providing systematic methods to implement complex, non-Clifford unitary operations using measurements and feedforward. This advances the understanding of universal quantum computation beyond simple gate sets.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the class of operations achievable using shallow quantum circuits augmented with measurements and feedforward (CMF protocols).
main_result: It establishes a general correspondence showing that CMF protocols are equivalent to designing protocols based on Quantum Error Correcting (QEC) codes, allowing for systematic construction of global unitaries.
method: The authors use QEC formalism, defining CMF isometries using circuits, measurement projectors, and feedforward unitaries, and relating this structure to code properties like error detectability.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum circuits implementing global unitary operations and state preparation, formalized using the structure of Quantum Error Correcting Codes (e.g., stabilizer codes, non-additive codes).
key_observables: The detectability of measurement errors on the codespace ($P E_a P = c_a P$) and the resulting non-Clifford nature of the target unitary operation are key observables.
important_parameters: The depth of the resulting unitary operation, the type of measurement (Pauli vs. non-Pauli), and the structure of the underlying QEC code (e.g., additive vs. non-additive).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the measurement process is deterministic, which requires the error projectors to be detectable on the codespace.
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a summary of figures, but they reference specific equations (e.g., Eq. 12, Eq. 17, Eq. 21, Eq. 27) that illustrate the derived CMF isometries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general correspondence between CMF protocols and QEC codes, then deriving specific constructions for stabilizer codes with Pauli measurements, and finally generalizing to non-Pauli measurements and non-additive codes to achieve non-Clifford operations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, systematic framework for designing quantum gates and state preparation protocols that go beyond the limitations of Clifford circuits, which is crucial for building fault-tolerant quantum computation.
